rationale: Romans 5:14 itself calls Adam a "pattern" (Greek typos) of the One to come, so the typological label is the New Testament text's own vocabulary, not an interpreter's inference; that is why the label is explicit. The Genesis side is anchored in the chapter's account of the man's act and its consequences (3:6, 3:17-19), not in 3:15. 1 Corinthians 15:21-22 and 15:45-49 extend the same Adam and Christ pairing but are not typed as a separate row because a range cannot span books. Schreiner (BECNT) is reported to call Romans 5:12-21 one of the hardest Pauline passages, so this row records that Paul draws the pairing, not how the two correspond; that page reference, like Moo's, comes through a secondary paper and needs checking against the commentaries.
